subject: Re: P-values for estimated effects from fitqtl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: P-values for estimated effects from fitqtl
parts:
> I'm using the R/QTL package to run a QTL mapping on F2 population.
>
> I used the fitqtl function to fit a model include 4 QTLs and to get the estimated effects (a and d) of each one of them.
>
> In the results table I see the estimated effects (a and d), the SE and the t value, as follow:
>
> Estimated effects:
> -----------------
> est SE t
> Intercept 25.51465 0.94540 26.988
> 4...@17.5a 3.45524 2.42703 1.424
> 4...@17.5d 4.11520 3.58640 1.147
> 4...@30.0a -3.86838 1.87349 -2.065
> 4...@30.0d -3.09783 3.07563 -1.007
> ......
>
> I want to get the P-value to each of the effects, but I'm not sure how many DF were considered in the analysis.

In considering the significance of QTL in a multiple QTL model, I would focus on the drop-one-QTL results from fitqtl. This gives p-values, but they don't account for the search across the genome, but are just point-wise. I focus on the LOD scores, instead, and compare them to the results of a permutation test with scanone() or scantwo().

karl
